text:
Anya: Spike summary — management-plane slicing (one mgmt-plane per tenant) vs centralized mgmt gateway for Private/VPC onboarding. Need tradeoffs + roll-forward plan.
Mike: quick take: per-tenant solves blast radius + auditing but multiplies certs, controllers, and route state.
Sarah: biggest ops concern is metrics + quota enforcement. If we go per-tenant we need per-tenant ingest pipelines or tagging at the gateway.
Joseph: hybrid option: per-tenant control-plane *stateful* controllers, but a thin centralized gateway for bootstrap and health checks. reduces per-tenant infra while keeping isolation.
Anya: can we get concrete failure modes? e.g., cert rotation, auth token theft, reconciliation storms.
Mike: cert rotation — per-tenant means rotated keys only impact that tenant; centralized means a compromise could affect everyone. Ops burden: we need automated rotation + observe/alert.
Sarah: routing/routing tables: per-tenant avoids complex route-table prefixes across accounts, but multiplies ENIs / NATs and increases IP churn. Centralized keeps stable egress but forces us to preserve src IP mapping for customers that require IP allowlists.
Joseph: cost math: baseline estimate for per-tenant control-plane N g4s per 100 tenants vs centralized 1 cluster with autoscale. My napkin math: per-tenant adds ~2.3x infra cost at our current scale.
Anya: what about rollout? Could we flip tenants gradually? How hard is migration from central -> per-tenant?
Mike: easiest path is central-first: onboard everyone to centralized mgmt gateway; for customers with strict isolation we spin up per-tenant mgmt-plane and cut routing + DNS to it. We need zero-downtime cutover plan and a read-only sync mode for state.
Sarah: observability note: we must tag traces by tenant id at the earliest hop. If central gateway does tagging, we can keep a single pipeline. If per-tenant, we need a federated trace ingest or aggregated collector.
Anya: security: KMS/HSM integration — per-tenant gives separate CMKs per customer, good for compliance. Centralized can still support per-tenant CMKs but increases key management complexity.
Joseph: network specifics: for centralized gateway we need predictable egress IPs. Example config snippet for centralized NAT approach: 
```
# central egress route example (aws)
RouteTableId: rt-0abcd
DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
NatGatewayId: nat-0fedcba
Tags: [{Key: TenantScoped, Value: "central"}]
```
This simplifies allowlist but creates capacity contention.
sre-bot: CPU pressure alert: gateway-prod-1 at 85% for 3m — FYI, might be related to integration test spike.
Mike: resilience: centralized gateway needs stronger throttles & per-tenant circuit breakers. Per-tenant relies on isolation by design.
Sarah: cost/observability/op risk summary: central = cheaper+simpler observability but higher blast radius; per-tenant = safer+compliant but higher cost and operational complexity.
Anya: proposal: ship centralized gateway as default + well-automated on-demand per-tenant mgmt plane for compliance customers. Action items: 1) Define per-tenant provisioning API (infra-as-code + cert bootstrap). 2) Design read-only state sync for cutover. 3) Add per-tenant rate-limits/circuits to central gateway. 4) Run a migration rehearsal with one willing customer.
Joseph: +1 to rehearsal. I can own the provisioning API spike.
Mike: I'll prototype the circuit-breaker and the cert rotation playbook.
Sarah: I'll draft the observability tagging and cost dashboard queries.
Anya: I'll write the rollout checklist and RFC follow-up. Thanks team! :thumbsup:
